title: Evidence Manifest

deterministicPayload.description: Canonicalizable content-derived state. Random UUIDs, timestamps, session identifiers, and UI state are prohibited here by contract and canonicalization tests.

x-acquisition-lineage-invariants: Every proposal node has one incoming package-to-proposal edge from a package linked to its request
Every proposal decision resolves to one proposal with the same proposalSha256
Every governed promoted fact resolves to an effective approved proposal decision for its proposalSha256
Every artifact SHA-256 cited by a proposal or promoted fact occurs in its linked acquisition payload reference and manifest artifacts
Every requesting-module identifier and rerun-trigger key remains connected from request through promoted fact
All acquisition lineage nodeId and edgeId values are unique and every edge endpoint resolves to exactly one node
Every promoted fact identifies one existing factKey and valid JSON Pointer in proposedExtractedFacts, and its factContentSha256 matches canonical {factKey, factJsonPointer, value}
Every promoted fact citationId resolves to a citation on the same proposal and its artifactSha256 occurs in that promoted fact
Promotion under a revoked or non-effective approval, ambiguous multi-fact promotion, and duplicate promotion to conflicting governed records are invalid
Orphan proposals, decisions without proposals, promoted facts without effective approval, mismatched artifact hashes, broken rerun-trigger lineage, and duplicate node identifiers are invalid
x-terminal-ledger-semantics: terminalDispositionLedger is accounting-only and cannot confer release, authority, approval, or a governed human-final disposition
accepted-for-processing means only that accounting processing may continue; provisional-safety-block and pending-human-disposition remain downstream blocked
US2 may balance reconciliation with provisional accounting categories while every governed record remains provisional
Only typed human decisions recorded separately in operationalMetadata establish released, final-quarantine, rejected, revoked, or superseded governed states
x-governed-decision-projection-invariant: EvidenceRelationship.status and normalized populationCandidate.candidateStatus are proposal-only and cannot store approved, rejected, revoked, superseded, released, or final-quarantine
ClassificationProposal.status is proposal-only; effective classification status is replayed from its typed human ClassificationApproval chain without mutating the proposal
Effective relationship and population-candidate status is a computed projection from the applicable gapless typed human decision chain and never mutates deterministic source evidence

Every decision chain preserves exact subject key, target identity where applicable, artifact SHA-256 values, decision type, decisionContentSha256, predecessor ID/content hash, rule-set/schema versions, and human actor

Orphan approval, system approval, missing decision, wrong decision type, wrong subject or target, stale or mismatched decision content hash, branch, cycle, gap, or ineffective/revoked/superseded approval blocks governed downstream use

Every PopulationCandidateDecision candidateKey resolves to exactly one populationCandidates source record in this manifest, whose recomputed candidateKey and artifactSha256 match; zero or multiple matches, changed content, or stale keys are invalid

Every population evidenceReference resolves by evidenceKey to exactly one populationEvidenceObservations entry with the same recomputed evidenceKey; the reference and observation agree exactly on artifactSha256, citationId, sourceLocator, evidenceKind, observedTextOrValue presence, and canonical bytes

Every populationEvidenceObservation evidenceKey and citationId is unique, its evidenceKey recomputes from its canonical deterministic content, and its artifactSha256 resolves to exactly one artifact in the manifest validated artifact set

Missing, zero/multiple, duplicate-key, duplicate-citation, artifact-mismatched, locator-mismatched, changed-content, stale-evidenceKey, unresolved-artifact, and incomplete-manifest population evidence is invalid
An incomplete manifest cannot claim an approved governed projection; downstream use requires replay to one current effective approved same-subject decision

UnresolvedItem deterministic source status is open or assigned only; resolved, accepted-risk, reopened, and superseded are computed projections available only through a complete effective UnresolvedItemDecision chain

Authority is effective only while its classificationApprovalId resolves to the current effective same-artifact classification approval with matching recomputed content hash; revocation, supersession, ineffectiveness, stale hashes, or changed bytes invalidate dependent authority, and renewal requires a new typed AuthorityDecision with current exact lineage
Exact-duplicate byte linkage may be established cryptographically through exactDuplicateOfSha256 but does not mutate EvidenceRelationship.status or constitute human governed approval
x-artifact-eligibility-invariants: Artifact downstreamEligibility stores only blocked, proposed-only, or pending-human-decision and never stores approved or another human-final value

Effective artifact eligibility is a computed projection from the current effective same-artifact ArtifactEligibilityDecision chain plus any applicable human quarantine/release chain and is never copied into deterministic artifact source evidence
Replay validates artifactSha256, decision type, decisionContentSha256, appendOrdinal, predecessor ID/content hash, effective state, and release/quarantine/revocation/supersession lineage
Missing/system/stale/mismatched/ineffective/revoked/branched/superseded decisions and incomplete manifests remain blocked
Changed bytes create a new artifact SHA-256 and decision lifecycle and can never inherit eligibility from prior bytes

x-deterministic-array-semantics.deterministicPayload.snapshot.entries: set-like; sort by NFC submittedPath, then sha256, then sizeBytes; reject duplicate submittedPath after path normalization
x-deterministic-array-semantics.deterministicPayload.artifacts: set-like; sort by artifactKey, then sha256; reject duplicate artifactKey
x-deterministic-array-semantics.deterministicPayload.containmentEdges: order-significant; preserve extraction sequence established by parent artifact then sequence; ties are invalid
x-deterministic-array-semantics.deterministicPayload.failedMemberObserva: order-significant; preserve extractor observation sequence by parent artifact then sequence; ties are invalid
x-deterministic-array-semantics.deterministicPayload.extractionResults: set-like; sort by source artifact SHA-256, source locator, then rule/method version and canonical item bytes; reject duplicate stable result keys
x-deterministic-array-semantics.deterministicPayload.screeningFindings: set-like; sort by findingKey then artifactSha256; reject duplicate findingKey
x-deterministic-array-semantics.deterministicPayload.screeningOutcomes: set-like; sort by outcomeKey then artifactSha256; reject duplicate outcomeKey
x-deterministic-array-semantics.deterministicPayload.classificationPropo: set-like; sort by proposalKey then artifactSha256; reject duplicate proposalKey
x-deterministic-array-semantics.deterministicPayload.evidenceRelationshi: set-like; sort by relationshipKey and canonical item bytes; reject duplicate relationshipKey
x-deterministic-array-semantics.deterministicPayload.populationEvidenceO: set-like; validate evidenceKey against canonical observation content, sort by evidenceKey, then citationId, artifactSha256, sourceLocator, and canonical item bytes; reject duplicate evidenceKey, duplicate citationId, duplicate canonical content, and indistinguishable normalized elements; null items and missing required registry are invalid
x-deterministic-array-semantics.deterministicPayload.populationCandidate: set-like; validate candidateKey against canonical candidate content, sort ascending by candidateKey then artifactSha256 and canonical item bytes, and reject duplicate candidateKey, duplicate canonical content, zero/multiple identity matches, stale keys, and indistinguishable normalized elements

intrinsic PopulationCandidate set-like rule; validate evidenceKey, sort ascending by evidenceKey then canonical item bytes, and reject duplicate keys/content and indistinguishable normalized elements; this identical rule applies in every embedding and overrides the generic recursive fallback
x-deterministic-array-semantics.deterministicPayload.unresolvedItems: set-like; sort by itemKey and canonical item bytes; reject duplicate itemKey
x-deterministic-array-semantics.deterministicPayload.validationResults: set-like; sort by validationKey and canonical item bytes; reject duplicate validationKey
x-deterministic-array-semantics.deterministicPayload.acquisitionPayloadR: set-like; sort by requestPayloadSha256, packagePayloadSha256, proposalPayloadSha256 with null before hashes; reject duplicate hash tuples
set-like; sort ascending lowercase hexadecimal; reject duplicates
x-deterministic-array-semantics.reconciliationTotals.originLedger: set-like; sort by recordId; reject duplicate recordId
x-deterministic-array-semantics.reconciliationTotals.terminalDisposition: set-like; sort by recordId; reject duplicate recordId

x-operational-lineage-array-ordering.operationalMetadata.acquisitionLineageNo: set-like projection; sort by nodeId then nodeType; reject duplicate nodeId; node contentSha256 follows node-type deterministic hash semantics
x-operational-lineage-array-ordering.operationalMetadata.acquisitionLineageEd: set-like projection; sort by edgeId then fromNodeId then toNodeId; reject duplicate edgeId
x-operational-lineage-array-ordering.operationalMetadata.proposalDecisionReco: order-significant append chain; sort/replay only by appendOrdinal and reject gaps, duplicates, branches, or cycles; timestamps never order the chain
x-operational-lineage-array-ordering.operationalMetadata.governedPromotedFact: set-like projection; sort by proposalSha256, factKey, factJsonPointer, targetGovernedRecordType, targetGovernedRecordId; reject conflicting duplicate promotion keys
x-operational-lineage-array-ordering.note: These operational container arrays are excluded from contentManifestId. Their referenced node/fact content hashes are deterministic and use the rules in evidence-acquisition.schema.json.

x-canonicalization-profile: PBGC Case Workbench Canonicalization Profile v1
x-numeric-canonicalization: The profile uses RFC 8785 number serialization for finite JSON numbers; equivalent notation hashes identically, negative zero serializes as 0, and NaN/infinities are invalid. Exact lexical decimals use governed-records canonicalDecimalString values.
x-recursive-deterministic-json: Object keys canonicalize recursively. Intrinsic type-level array rules, including PopulationCandidate.evidence, apply in every embedding and take precedence over generic fallback. Arrays at exact registered paths use those rules. Every otherwise-unregistered array nested at any depth in deterministic manifest values or referenced deterministic records is order-significant by default and preserves element order. Exact path rules override only their exact array scope.
